name: tool-result-parts-mint-tool-message
description: a TOOL_CALL_RESULT whose content is a list of parts mints a tool message carrying those parts unchanged, placed after the assistant message that made the call, with no warning; asserted on the assembled messages, because the two clients deliver a different event granularity to application code
kill: make the TOOL_CALL_RESULT reducer flatten or stringify a parts array before storing it as the tool message's content

dotnet.intentional: the .NET client assembles history through Microsoft.Extensions.AI ChatMessages, and a FunctionResultContent holds one result object: the tool result's parts are flattened to their text (AGUIContent.ToString) and the tool message takes the tool call's id, so the document part does not survive into the assembled messages. The event itself carries the parts — AGUIToolMessage and ToolCallResultEvent hold AGUIContent — and a parts-preserving mapping onto MEAI DataContent/UriContent is tracked separately. The flattening is lossy, and the specification asks a consumer to announce a lossy rendering rather than let a dropped part look like one the producer never sent, so .NET warns once for the result — which is why `noWarnings` cannot hold on this lane and is replaced by the warning it does emit. TypeScript keeps the parts and so has nothing to announce.
warnings: The result of tool call 'toolparts-c1' was flattened to text
